answer: Admission is a jetty one seat wide: each epoch's pulse opens a short crossing window, and every crossing dissolves one passage through a karst of single-use channels. No tunnel survives reuse, so 900 clones cannot share one; each needs its own channel, its own bond, and a proof seeded by that epoch's beacon. Channels fed from one upstream source collapse together: correlation triggers joint slashing, one detected fault kills the batch. Expected cost to keep a 900-clone farm alive is super-linear - every new sibling raises the odds the whole correlated batch is wiped.
